entries.title: Executable identity, stock launcher and Bun bootstrap ordering
entries.priority_reason: Launch identity is a small compatibility boundary; Bun-specific workarounds should remain runtime-specific rather than inflate the native gap.

entries.title: ICE distribution preflight, early agent commands and builtin factory order
entries.priority_reason: Distribution policy and subagent integrations must be installed before user extensions and session execution; a parser-only port does not provide this behavior.

entries.title: Argument token grammar, complete flag surface and diagnostic semantics
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect token consumption can discard a user prompt or reinterpret options; missing flag names are only part of the actual parser gap.

entries.title: Run-mode resolution and metadata short-circuit precedence
entries.priority_reason: Metadata and mode precedence affect scripts, startup side effects and protocol ownership; stale comments currently obscure implemented native behavior.

entries.title: Cwd-bound runtime factory, trust staging and startup service composition
entries.priority_reason: Startup service composition determines which project code and policy enter a session; wrong cwd or trust staging creates functional and authority mismatches.

entries.title: Startup session selection, exact-ID validation, naming and missing-cwd recovery
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect session precedence or cwd selection can append to the wrong conversation or execute in an unintended project; naming timing is independently tested.

entries.title: CLI model, thinking, fast-mode and tool-option precedence
entries.priority_reason: Model/scope precedence changes the provider used for a prompt and currently mutates saved native scope unexpectedly compared with TS.

entries.title: Piped stdin ownership, complete-input collection and read failures
entries.priority_reason: Silently dropping a failed piped prompt can execute an unintended partial request; complete-input semantics are directly covered by TS test source.

entries.title: CLI file attachments, typed text failures and image preprocessing
entries.priority_reason: Attachment preprocessing controls usable image dimensions, format support and prompt provenance; native raw-image support is present but incomplete.

entries.title: Initial prompt concatenation and remaining-message ownership
entries.priority_reason: The live native assembly already matches the meaningful startup behavior; only helper representation/empty-option edges differ.

entries.title: Credential-print command grammar, output discipline and duration parsing defect
entries.priority_reason: Scripts need a deterministic credential-only command; parser errors and incidental startup output can otherwise break integrations or expose diagnostics.

entries.title: Credential-print provider inference, refresh policy and ambiguity handling
entries.priority_reason: Returning a credential from the wrong provider or skipping refresh breaks consumers; the inference and failure rules are more specific than ordinary auth readiness checks.

entries.title: Credential startup migration and recoverable native layout migration
entries.priority_reason: Migration failure can strand credentials or remove their last normal lookup location; startup must remain recoverable without silently claiming success.

entries.title: Session, managed-binary, prompt-directory and keybinding startup migrations
entries.priority_reason: Legacy users need predictable migration, but the current functions contain swallowed failures and a Windows path defect that should not be preserved.

entries.title: Official first-run gate and startup theme bootstrap
entries.priority_reason: Onboarding is conditional rather than a universal startup gap, but terminal lifetime and preference persistence need precise behavior.

entries.title: Startup selectors, config wrapper and resume-picker terminal lifetime
entries.priority_reason: A native resume picker exists, but startup configuration and consistent temporary-terminal cleanup need additional integration.

entries.title: Available-model listing, fuzzy filtering and stable tabular output
entries.priority_reason: Both list models, but filtering and availability semantics differ enough to mislead users about which model can actually run.

entries.title: Exact identity helpers, canonical paths and deliberately limited legacy compatibility
entries.priority_reason: The main audit correction is avoiding an invented migration feature; actual alias support and small identity boundaries remain important.

entries.title: Offline normalization, startup diagnostics, output ownership and shutdown integration
entries.priority_reason: Startup output contamination and mismatched cleanup can break RPC/scripts; several native lifecycle pieces already exist and should be preserved.

candidate_exclusions.reason: Mechanical indexed-env-read classification is false: this line assigns restored names into process.env. The actual environment restoration/write contract and raw /proc input are covered by CLI-001; no independent environment lookup exists at this candidate.

claims.claim: Package resource selector is missing in native.
claims.finding: TS selectConfig owns temporary terminal startup, scope parameters and stop/watch cleanup; its resource mutations are TUI-068/069 and package routing is the package supplement. Native startup dispatcher has no equivalent config command wrapper, but native generic session/settings selectors are real and should not be called absent.

claims.claim: --fast/--no-fast are absent from native args and request the priority tier.
claims.verdict: confirmed parser gap; downstream behavior delegated
claims.finding: Native parser lacks these builtin spellings. TS carries a defined true/false fastMode through buildSessionOptions; actual provider/session support and service-tier behavior belongs to SESSION/AI, so a parser flag alone is not completion.

The flag grammar is bare true or Number-converted integer1..65535; it adds an optional dashboard to an always-on recorder rather than enabling all observability. OBS-003/014/016 own the native service gap.

claims.claim: --print-system-template prints the template and exits; missing in native.
claims.finding: TS outputs DEFAULT_BASE_TEMPLATE plus LF after parser-error/version checks and before export/migrations/runtime. Native has debug-system-prompt but no same builtin flag/output route.

claims.verdict: qualified: spelling/default/validation differ, native mode exists
claims.finding: Native --tui-mode supports regular/fullscreen, case-insensitively, with platform-specific default. The exact TS --ui-mode spelling is not builtin; that does not mean the native renderer lacks either mode. TUI owns actual renderer differences.

claims.claim: ICE guarded-mode/subagent flags and agents/import-pack commands are missing from native.
claims.verdict: caller routing confirmed; authority semantics cross-owned
claims.finding: The ICE wrapper explicitly runs import-pack and agents early, validates normalized distribution flags and installs four builtin integrations. Native app has different early commands. Full policy/agent-definition semantics are SUB and SAFE ownership, with CLI-002 tracking the actual invocation/order.

claims.claim: Legacy compatibility maps old pi/ice environment variables, paths and extension names and is irrelevant until users migrate.
claims.finding: Current env/path/identity helpers intentionally do not promote historical namespaces or discover .pi trees. They use exact own names, shallow copies and canonical path joins. Fourteen exact module aliases and concrete startup migrations remain active current behavior. Migration failures require repair, not a blanket n/a label.

claims.claim: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR bridge lets Pi packages use ICE state; Rust cannot load Pi TS packages.
claims.verdict: TS marker confirmed; categorical native claim requires bridge-specific comparison
claims.finding: TS uses nullish assignment and preserves an existing empty value. This marker is not broad home-state import. Native package/bridge capability must be determined by EXT-001/002 and the package supplement; the absence of this launcher assignment does not prove all native Pi interoperation impossible.

open_questions.question: Should the native compatibility surface retain stricter missing-value diagnostics, --tui-mode/platform default and unauthenticated catalog listing, or expose explicit aliases/options for the TS spellings and available-model mode? Both current behaviors are documented; no undocumented default is assumed.

What mode-aware authorization interface should replace TS's unguarded cross-project readline prompt, and at what trust stage should project commands→prompts migration occur? The current source order is documented; no policy change was executed.

Implementation should repair the documented uppercase duration, pre-publication credential mutation, Windows basename and async dialog-finalization defects rather than preserving them as compatibility requirements. Coordinator to record chosen native behavior during implementation planning.
